findings.evidence: template/scripts/agent_friction.py `evidence_source_status` parses every line of the whole log with no recency window, while `ambiguous_attribution_events` uses a 14-day window. `require_checkpoint` re-evaluates the gap on every call. A stale historic bad line therefore becomes permanent ceremony and weakens the 'clean task stays one command' goal. Consider scoping the check to the retention window or to the lines that `read_events` actually skips.
findings.summary: A single malformed line anywhere in the shared friction log makes `evidence_source_status` return `partial`. That forces `--accept-gap friction-log` on every later task and Requirement checkpoint until the log is hand-edited.

findings.evidence: tests/test_retrospective_attribution.py `test_lost_task_attribution_is_recovered_from_branch_and_source_issue` uses `run={"source_issue": BRANCH}`. `task_aliases` (agent_friction.py) imports `managed_task.read_task_state` and swallows all exceptions, returning an empty set. Any import failure or a key or format mismatch between `state["source_issue"]` and `run.source_issue` would silently disable inference with no signal.
findings.summary: The managed-task source-issue alias path is the real #284 recovery case, but no test exercises it. The 'by-issue' test sets `run.source_issue` equal to the branch name instead of going through `task_aliases`.

findings.evidence: `default_attribution` returns (None, 'unattributed') for main. `event_identities` excludes the main branch name. `ambiguous_attribution_events` is not filtered by task, so `ambiguous_attribution_not_attributed` lands in every checkpoint result in the repo. This is informational only, but it adds noise to the otherwise short path.
findings.summary: Events recorded on the integration branch without `--task` are now stored as `unattributed` with branch `main`. They count as 'ambiguous' for 14 days and are printed on every unrelated task's review-path and checkpoint output.

findings.evidence: docs/engineering/agent-workflow.md line 43 (and the .jinja equivalent) still says `--result none` requires 'every current-task high-signal lifecycle failure has an explicit disposition' and that `--lifecycle-disposition` is 'for the resolved/already-recorded cases'. The new text makes `--disposition` canonical, adds `expected-behavior`, and covers all mandatory signals.
findings.summary: The retained paragraph in the central and template workflow docs still describes the old narrower semantics. That contradicts the new paragraphs added just above it.
